chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Do not ask about that which may not happen, for in that which has already happened, you have enough to occupy you.

key_terms.الشُّغُل: occupations / concerns / affairs that occupy one's attention
key_terms.لَا يَكُونُ: that which may not happen / future uncertainty

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali advise regarding worrying about future uncertain events?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises against excessive curiosity or worry about future uncertain events, noting that one already has sufficient concerns from past and present affairs to occupy their mind. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *hazm al-amr* (prudence) and focusing on actionable duties rather than speculative *ghayb* (unseen), a principle often cited in discussions on mental discipline and spiritual focus. It serves as a practical guide for avoiding the anxiety of the unknown while remaining engaged with the tangible responsibilities of the present.
